insight: Iran's performance in the 2026 World Cup has been notably influenced by hydration breaks, with the team gaining momentum in 4 out of 6 breaks, indicating a slight increase in their overall pace of play. However, when Iran was pressing before a hydration break, they tended to lose momentum, with their pace of play decreasing by an average of 0.100 minutes, and they were unable to regain it after the break in either instance. In contrast, when Iran was not pressing before a break, they were able to maintain a higher pace of play, with an average increase of 0.125 minutes, suggesting that the team is able to recharge and refocus during these stops. Overall, the data suggests that hydration breaks have a positive impact on Iran's performance, particularly when they are not exerting themselves intensely before the break.
